stages.label: KS3
stages.sub: National Curriculum for England · Key Stage 3 Chemistry
stages.source: Follows the chemistry content of the National Curriculum for England at Key Stage 3, in the order of its own headings.

lectures.title: Solids, liquids and gases
lectures.blurb: Describe the three states of matter and explain their properties with the particle model.

lectures.title: Gas pressure
lectures.blurb: Explain what causes gas pressure and what makes it change.

lectures.title: Changes of state
lectures.blurb: Name the changes of state and explain them with particles.

lectures.title: Atoms and the Dalton model
lectures.blurb: Describe Dalton's model of the atom and what it explains.

lectures.title: Atoms, elements and compounds
lectures.blurb: Tell atoms, molecules, elements, compounds and mixtures apart.

lectures.title: Chemical symbols and formulae
lectures.blurb: Read and write symbols and formulae, and name simple compounds.

lectures.title: Conservation of mass
lectures.blurb: Use conservation of mass in changes of state and chemical reactions.

lectures.title: Pure substances
lectures.blurb: Say what pure means in chemistry and how to identify a pure substance.

lectures.title: Mixtures and dissolving
lectures.blurb: Use the words solute, solvent, solution and solubility, and explain dissolving with particles.

lectures.title: Diffusion
lectures.blurb: Explain diffusion with the particle model and say what changes its speed.

lectures.title: Filtration, evaporation and distillation
lectures.blurb: Choose and describe the right method to separate a mixture.

lectures.title: Chromatography
lectures.blurb: Carry out paper chromatography and read a chromatogram.

lectures.title: Rearranging atoms
lectures.blurb: Tell a chemical reaction from a physical change and spot the signs of a reaction.

lectures.title: Word and symbol equations
lectures.blurb: Write word equations and simple balanced symbol equations.

lectures.title: Combustion and oxidation
lectures.blurb: Describe burning, complete and incomplete combustion, and oxidation.

lectures.title: Thermal decomposition and displacement
lectures.blurb: Describe thermal decomposition and predict displacement reactions.

lectures.title: Acids, alkalis and the pH scale
lectures.blurb: Use indicators and the pH scale to classify solutions.

lectures.title: Neutralisation and salts
lectures.blurb: Describe the reactions of acids with alkalis and with metals, and name the salt made.

lectures.title: Catalysts
lectures.blurb: Explain what a catalyst does and give examples.

lectures.title: Energy and changes of state
lectures.blurb: Describe the energy changes when a substance changes state.

lectures.title: Exothermic and endothermic reactions
lectures.blurb: Classify reactions as exothermic or endothermic from temperature changes.

lectures.title: Mendeleev's Periodic Table
lectures.blurb: Explain how Mendeleev arranged the elements and why his table was accepted.

lectures.title: Periods, groups, metals and non-metals
lectures.blurb: Find your way around the Periodic Table.

lectures.title: Properties of metals and non-metals
lectures.blurb: Compare the physical properties of metals and non-metals.

lectures.title: Patterns and predictions
lectures.blurb: Use the trends in Groups 1, 7 and 0 to predict properties and reactions.

lectures.title: Metal and non-metal oxides
lectures.blurb: Explain why metal oxides are basic and non-metal oxides are acidic.

lectures.title: The reactivity series
lectures.blurb: Place metals and carbon in order of reactivity using evidence from reactions.

lectures.title: Extracting metals with carbon
lectures.blurb: Explain how carbon is used to get metals from their oxides.

lectures.title: Ceramics, polymers and composites
lectures.blurb: Compare the properties and uses of ceramics, polymers and composites.

lectures.title: The structure and composition of the Earth
lectures.blurb: Describe the layers of the Earth and what the crust is made of.

lectures.title: The rock cycle
lectures.blurb: Explain how igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks form and change.

lectures.title: Resources and recycling
lectures.blurb: Explain why Earth's resources are limited and judge how well recycling works.

lectures.title: The carbon cycle
lectures.blurb: Describe how carbon moves between the air, living things, the oceans and rocks.

lectures.title: The atmosphere and climate
lectures.blurb: State the composition of the air and explain how human activity changes the climate.

stages.label: IGCSE
stages.source: Checked against the official Cambridge syllabus for exams in 2026 to 2028. Topic numbers match the syllabus.

lectures.title: Solids, liquids and gases
lectures.blurb: Describe the three states with the particle model, and explain changes of state and gas pressure.

lectures.title: Diffusion
lectures.blurb: Explain diffusion with moving particles, and why lighter molecules diffuse faster.

lectures.title: Elements, compounds and mixtures
lectures.blurb: Tell elements, compounds and mixtures apart.

lectures.title: Atomic structure and the Periodic Table
lectures.blurb: Describe the atom, work out electronic configurations and link them to the Periodic Table.

lectures.title: Isotopes
lectures.blurb: Define isotopes and calculate relative atomic mass from abundances.

lectures.title: Ions and ionic bonds
lectures.blurb: Explain how ions form, draw dot-and-cross diagrams and explain the properties of ionic compounds.

lectures.title: Simple molecules and covalent bonds
lectures.blurb: Draw the bonding in simple molecules and explain their low melting points.

lectures.title: Giant covalent structures
lectures.blurb: Relate the structures of diamond, graphite and silicon(IV) oxide to their uses.

lectures.title: Metallic bonding
lectures.blurb: Describe metallic bonding and use it to explain how metals behave.

lectures.title: Formulae
lectures.blurb: Write formulae and balanced equations, including ionic equations and state symbols.

lectures.title: Relative masses of atoms and molecules
lectures.blurb: Define and calculate relative atomic and relative molecular mass.

lectures.title: The mole and the Avogadro constant
lectures.blurb: Do every kind of mole calculation: masses, gas volumes, solutions, yield and purity.

lectures.title: Electrolysis
lectures.blurb: Predict and explain the products of electrolysis, and write the half-equations.

lectures.title: Hydrogen–oxygen fuel cells
lectures.blurb: Describe a hydrogen–oxygen fuel cell and weigh it against a petrol engine.

lectures.title: Exothermic and endothermic reactions
lectures.blurb: Draw reaction pathway diagrams and calculate enthalpy changes from bond energies.

lectures.title: Physical and chemical changes
lectures.blurb: Tell a physical change from a chemical change.

lectures.title: Rate of reaction
lectures.blurb: Explain what changes the rate of a reaction using collision theory, and measure rates by experiment.

lectures.title: Reversible reactions and equilibrium
lectures.blurb: Predict how conditions shift an equilibrium, and explain the Haber and Contact processes.

lectures.title: Redox
lectures.blurb: Identify oxidation and reduction using oxygen, electrons and oxidation numbers.

lectures.title: The characteristic properties of acids and bases
lectures.blurb: Describe the reactions of acids and bases, the pH scale, and strong and weak acids.

lectures.title: Oxides
lectures.blurb: Classify oxides as acidic, basic or amphoteric.

lectures.title: Preparation of salts
lectures.blurb: Choose and describe the right method to make any salt, using the solubility rules.

lectures.title: Arrangement of elements
lectures.blurb: Explain how the Periodic Table is arranged and what the position of an element tells you.

lectures.title: Group I properties
lectures.blurb: Describe the alkali metals and the trends down the group.

lectures.title: Group VII properties
lectures.blurb: Describe the halogens, their trends and their displacement reactions.

lectures.title: Transition elements
lectures.blurb: State the typical properties of transition elements.

lectures.title: Noble gases
lectures.blurb: Explain why the noble gases are unreactive.

lectures.title: Properties of metals
lectures.blurb: Compare the physical and chemical properties of metals and non-metals.

lectures.title: Uses of metals
lectures.blurb: Link the uses of aluminium and copper to their properties.

lectures.title: Alloys and their properties
lectures.blurb: Explain why alloys are harder and stronger than pure metals.

lectures.title: Reactivity series
lectures.blurb: Use the reactivity series to predict reactions, and deduce an order from experiments.

lectures.title: Corrosion of metals
lectures.blurb: Explain rusting and how barrier methods, galvanising and sacrificial protection stop it.

lectures.title: Extraction of metals
lectures.blurb: Describe how iron is made in the blast furnace and aluminium by electrolysis.

lectures.title: Water
lectures.blurb: Test for water, and describe how the water supply is treated.

lectures.title: Fertilisers
lectures.blurb: Explain why fertilisers contain nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium.

lectures.title: Air quality and climate
lectures.blurb: Describe the air, its pollutants and their sources, and the causes of climate change.

lectures.title: Formulae, functional groups and terminology
lectures.blurb: Use displayed, structural and general formulae, and define homologous series and isomers.

lectures.title: Naming organic compounds
lectures.blurb: Name and draw alkanes, alkenes, alcohols, carboxylic acids and esters.

lectures.title: Fuels
lectures.blurb: Describe fractional distillation of petroleum and the uses of the fractions.

lectures.title: Alkanes
lectures.blurb: Describe the bonding and reactions of alkanes, including substitution with chlorine.

lectures.title: Alkenes
lectures.blurb: Describe cracking, the test for unsaturation and the addition reactions of alkenes.

lectures.title: Alcohols
lectures.blurb: Compare the two ways of making ethanol, and describe its reactions and uses.

lectures.title: Carboxylic acids
lectures.blurb: Describe the reactions of ethanoic acid and how esters are made.

lectures.title: Polymers
lectures.blurb: Draw addition and condensation polymers from their monomers, and discuss plastics and proteins.

lectures.title: Experimental design
lectures.blurb: Choose the right apparatus, and use the words for solutions correctly.

lectures.title: Acid–base titrations
lectures.blurb: Describe how to carry out a titration and identify the end-point.

lectures.title: Chromatography
lectures.blurb: Run and interpret paper chromatograms and calculate Rf values.

lectures.title: Separation and purification
lectures.blurb: Choose a separation method and judge purity from melting and boiling points.

lectures.title: Identification of ions and gases
lectures.blurb: Recall the tests for anions, cations and gases, and their results.

stages.label: AS Level
stages.source: Cambridge International AS & A Level Chemistry 9701, checked against the official syllabus for 2025 to 2027. Topic numbers match the syllabus.

lectures.title: Particles in the atom and atomic radius
lectures.blurb: Describe protons, neutrons and electrons, and explain trends in atomic and ionic radius.

lectures.title: Isotopes
lectures.blurb: Define isotopes and explain why they share chemical properties.

lectures.title: Electrons, energy levels and atomic orbitals
lectures.blurb: Write electronic configurations with s, p and d orbitals and describe orbital shapes.

lectures.title: Ionisation energy
lectures.blurb: Explain the trends in ionisation energy and deduce a group from successive ionisation energies.

lectures.title: Relative masses of atoms and molecules
lectures.blurb: Define relative atomic, isotopic, molecular and formula mass on the carbon-12 scale.

lectures.title: The mole and the Avogadro constant
lectures.blurb: Define the mole in terms of the Avogadro constant.

lectures.title: Formulas
lectures.blurb: Write formulae and balanced equations, and find empirical and molecular formulae.

lectures.title: Reacting masses and volumes (of solutions and gases)
lectures.blurb: Calculate with moles for masses, gas volumes and solutions, including titrations.

lectures.title: Electronegativity and bonding
lectures.blurb: Define electronegativity, explain its trends and use it to predict bond type.

lectures.title: Ionic bonding
lectures.blurb: Define ionic bonding and describe it in common compounds.

lectures.title: Metallic bonding
lectures.blurb: Define metallic bonding as attraction between positive ions and delocalised electrons.

lectures.title: Covalent bonding and coordinate (dative covalent) bonding
lectures.blurb: Describe covalent and dative bonds, σ and π bonds, hybridisation, bond energy and bond length.

lectures.title: Shapes of molecules
lectures.blurb: Predict shapes and bond angles using electron-pair repulsion theory.

lectures.title: Intermolecular forces, electronegativity and bond properties
lectures.blurb: Explain hydrogen bonding, dipoles and van der Waals' forces, and the odd properties of water.

lectures.title: Dot-and-cross diagrams
lectures.blurb: Draw dot-and-cross diagrams for ions and molecules, including expanded octets.

lectures.title: The gaseous state: ideal and real gases and pV = nRT
lectures.blurb: Explain gas pressure, state the assumptions of an ideal gas and use pV = nRT.

lectures.title: Bonding and structure
lectures.blurb: Describe the four kinds of lattice and deduce structure from physical properties.

lectures.title: Enthalpy change, ΔH
lectures.blurb: Define the standard enthalpy changes and calculate them from experiments and bond energies.

lectures.title: Hess's law
lectures.blurb: Use Hess's law and energy cycles to find enthalpy changes that cannot be measured.

lectures.title: Redox processes: electron transfer and changes in oxidation number (oxidation state)
lectures.blurb: Work out oxidation numbers, balance redox equations and name oxidising and reducing agents.

lectures.title: Chemical equilibria: reversible reactions, dynamic equilibrium
lectures.blurb: Apply Le Chatelier's principle, and calculate Kc and Kp.

lectures.title: Brønsted–Lowry theory of acids and bases
lectures.blurb: Describe acids and bases as proton donors and acceptors, and sketch pH titration curves.

lectures.title: Rate of reaction
lectures.blurb: Explain rate with collision theory and find a rate from experimental data.

lectures.title: Effect of temperature on reaction rates and the concept of activation energy
lectures.blurb: Use the Boltzmann distribution to explain the effect of temperature.

lectures.title: Homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysts
lectures.blurb: Explain how a catalyst works using the Boltzmann distribution and a reaction pathway diagram.

lectures.title: Periodicity of physical properties of the elements in Period 3
lectures.blurb: Explain the trends in radius, melting point and conductivity across Period 3.

lectures.title: Periodicity of chemical properties of the elements in Period 3
lectures.blurb: Describe the oxides, chlorides and hydroxides of Period 3 and explain their behaviour with water.

lectures.title: Chemical periodicity of other elements
lectures.blurb: Predict the properties of an element from its position, and identify an unknown element.

lectures.title: Similarities and trends in the properties of the Group 2 metals, magnesium to barium, and their compounds
lectures.blurb: Describe the reactions of the Group 2 metals and compounds, and the trends in solubility and thermal stability.

lectures.title: Physical properties of the Group 17 elements
lectures.blurb: Describe the colours and volatility of the halogens and explain the trend.

lectures.title: The chemical properties of the halogen elements and the hydrogen halides
lectures.blurb: Compare the halogens as oxidising agents and the thermal stability of the hydrogen halides.

lectures.title: Some reactions of the halide ions
lectures.blurb: Compare the halide ions as reducing agents, and test for them with silver nitrate.

lectures.title: The reactions of chlorine
lectures.blurb: Describe the disproportionation of chlorine and its use in water treatment.

lectures.title: Nitrogen and sulfur
lectures.blurb: Explain why nitrogen is unreactive, and describe ammonia, nitrogen oxides and acid rain.

topics.title: An introduction to AS Level organic chemistry

lectures.title: Formulas, functional groups and the naming of organic compounds
lectures.blurb: Use the six kinds of formula and name compounds of every AS functional group.

lectures.title: Characteristic organic reactions
lectures.blurb: Use the vocabulary of mechanisms: free radical, nucleophile, electrophile, and curly arrows.

lectures.title: Shapes of organic molecules; σ and π bonds
lectures.blurb: Explain the shapes of organic molecules with sp, sp² and sp³ hybridisation.

lectures.title: Isomerism: structural isomerism and stereoisomerism
lectures.blurb: Identify structural, geometrical and optical isomers and chiral centres.

lectures.title: Alkanes
lectures.blurb: Describe combustion, cracking and the free-radical substitution of alkanes.

lectures.title: Alkenes
lectures.blurb: Describe the addition reactions of alkenes, the electrophilic addition mechanism and Markovnikov's rule.

lectures.title: Halogenoalkanes
lectures.blurb: Describe nucleophilic substitution (SN1 and SN2) and elimination in halogenoalkanes.

lectures.title: Alcohols
lectures.blurb: Describe how alcohols are made and how they react, and classify them as primary, secondary or tertiary.

lectures.title: Aldehydes and ketones
lectures.blurb: Describe the reactions of aldehydes and ketones, and the tests that tell them apart.

lectures.title: Carboxylic acids
lectures.blurb: Describe how carboxylic acids are made and their reactions as acids.

lectures.title: Esters
lectures.blurb: Describe how esters are made and hydrolysed.

lectures.title: Primary amines
lectures.blurb: Describe how primary amines are made from halogenoalkanes.

lectures.title: Nitriles and hydroxynitriles
lectures.blurb: Describe how nitriles and hydroxynitriles are made and hydrolysed.

lectures.title: Addition polymerisation
lectures.blurb: Draw addition polymers and their repeat units, and discuss the disposal of polymers.

lectures.title: Organic synthesis
lectures.blurb: Plan multi-step routes between AS functional groups and analyse a given route.

lectures.title: Infrared spectroscopy
lectures.blurb: Identify functional groups from an infrared spectrum.

lectures.title: Mass spectrometry
lectures.blurb: Use a mass spectrum to find relative atomic mass, molecular mass and fragments.

stages.label: A Level
stages.source: Cambridge International AS & A Level Chemistry 9701, checked against the official syllabus for 2025 to 2027. Topic numbers match the syllabus.

lectures.title: Lattice energy and Born–Haber cycles
lectures.blurb: Define lattice energy, build Born–Haber cycles and explain what changes lattice energy.

lectures.title: Enthalpies of solution and hydration
lectures.blurb: Link enthalpy of solution, lattice energy and enthalpy of hydration in an energy cycle.

lectures.title: Entropy change, ΔS
lectures.blurb: Define entropy, predict the sign of an entropy change and calculate it.

lectures.title: Gibbs free energy change, ΔG
lectures.blurb: Use ΔG = ΔH − TΔS to decide whether a reaction is feasible.

lectures.title: Electrolysis
lectures.blurb: Predict the products of electrolysis and calculate amounts with Q = It and the Faraday constant.

lectures.title: Standard electrode potentials E⦵, standard cell potentials E⦵cell and the Nernst equation
lectures.blurb: Use standard electrode potentials to predict reactions and calculate cell potentials.

lectures.title: Acids and bases
lectures.blurb: Calculate pH for strong and weak acids, bases and buffers, and use Ka, Kw and Ksp.

lectures.title: Partition coefficients
lectures.blurb: Define and calculate a partition coefficient.

lectures.title: Simple rate equations, orders of reaction and rate constants
lectures.blurb: Find orders and rate constants from data, and link a rate equation to a mechanism.

lectures.title: Homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysts
lectures.blurb: Explain how named catalysts work, in one phase and at a surface.

lectures.title: Similarities and trends in the properties of the Group 2 metals, magnesium to barium, and their compounds
lectures.blurb: Explain the trends in thermal stability and solubility of Group 2 compounds.

lectures.title: General physical and chemical properties of the first row of transition elements, titanium to copper
lectures.blurb: Define a transition element and explain variable oxidation states, complexes and catalysis.

lectures.title: General characteristic chemical properties of the first set of transition elements, titanium to copper
lectures.blurb: Describe ligands, complexes, their shapes, ligand exchange and redox titrations.

lectures.title: Colour of complexes
lectures.blurb: Explain why transition element complexes are coloured, using d-orbital splitting.

lectures.title: Stereoisomerism in transition element complexes
lectures.blurb: Identify geometrical and optical isomers of complexes.

lectures.title: Stability constants, Kstab
lectures.blurb: Write and use stability constants to explain ligand exchange.

topics.title: An introduction to A Level organic chemistry

lectures.title: Formulas, functional groups and the naming of organic compounds
lectures.blurb: Name and draw the A Level functional groups, including arenes, phenols, acyl chlorides, amides and amino acids.

lectures.title: Characteristic organic reactions
lectures.blurb: Describe electrophilic substitution and addition–elimination.

lectures.title: Shapes of aromatic organic molecules; σ and π bonds
lectures.blurb: Describe the bonding and shape of benzene.

lectures.title: Isomerism: optical
lectures.blurb: Explain optical activity, racemic mixtures and why chirality matters in drugs.

lectures.title: Arenes
lectures.blurb: Describe the reactions of benzene and methylbenzene and the mechanism of electrophilic substitution.

lectures.title: Halogen compounds
lectures.blurb: Compare the reactivity of halogenoarenes with halogenoalkanes.

lectures.title: Alcohols
lectures.blurb: Describe the reaction of alcohols with acyl chlorides and compare acidities.

lectures.title: Phenol
lectures.blurb: Describe the reactions of phenol and explain its acidity and reactivity.

lectures.title: Carboxylic acids
lectures.blurb: Explain the relative acidity of carboxylic acids and describe their further oxidation.

lectures.title: Esters
lectures.blurb: Describe how esters are made from acyl chlorides.

lectures.title: Acyl chlorides
lectures.blurb: Describe the reactions of acyl chlorides and the addition–elimination mechanism.

lectures.title: Primary and secondary amines
lectures.blurb: Describe how amines are made and how they react.

lectures.title: Phenylamine and azo compounds
lectures.blurb: Describe how phenylamine is made, its reactions and the making of azo dyes.

lectures.title: Amides
lectures.blurb: Describe how amides are made, hydrolysed and reduced.

lectures.title: Amino acids
lectures.blurb: Describe zwitterions, peptide bonds and electrophoresis.

lectures.title: Condensation polymerisation
lectures.blurb: Describe polyesters and polyamides and draw their repeat units.

lectures.title: Predicting the type of polymerisation
lectures.blurb: Decide whether a monomer forms an addition or a condensation polymer, and work back from a polymer.

lectures.title: Degradable polymers
lectures.blurb: Explain why some polymers break down and others do not.

lectures.title: Organic synthesis
lectures.blurb: Plan multi-step syntheses across all functional groups and analyse a given route.

lectures.title: Thin-layer chromatography
lectures.blurb: Explain thin-layer chromatography and use Rf values.

lectures.title: Gas / liquid chromatography
lectures.blurb: Explain gas–liquid chromatography and use retention times and peak areas.

lectures.title: Carbon-13 NMR spectroscopy
lectures.blurb: Predict and interpret carbon-13 NMR spectra.

lectures.title: Proton (¹H) NMR spectroscopy
lectures.blurb: Predict and interpret proton NMR spectra, including splitting patterns.
